alt: A left-to-right picture. A buyer with a wallet creates a transaction, it is hashed, copied to four linked databases shown with a chain and a tick, and the seller receives it. Captions under each step say the transaction is distributed, validated, committed and miners are rewarded.
author: B140970324

alt: Alice signs the message Hello Bob with her private key. The signed message goes to Bob, who checks it with Alice's public key and gets True, meaning the message is authentic.
author: FlippyFlink

alt: Three transaction boxes in a row. Each holds the next owner's public key and the previous owner's signature. The signature is made by hashing the previous transaction with the next owner's public key and signing with the previous owner's private key.
author: Graingert

alt: Three blocks, 10, 11 and 12, in a row. Each shows Prev_Hash, Timestamp, Tx_Root and Nonce, with an arrow from each block to the next. Under block 11 a small tree of hashes of transactions Tx0 to Tx3 leads up to its Tx_Root.
author: Matthäus Wander

alt: A block explorer page for Bitcoin block 175418. The top lists its hash, previous block hash, time, difficulty, number of transactions, size, Merkle root and nonce. Below is a table of transactions with their inputs and outputs, and the first one is the coinbase generation transaction.
author: Cloudswrest

alt: The raw bytes of the Bitcoin genesis block in hexadecimal on a black background. The text column on the right reads The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.
author: Alhadis (vectorization); original by Satoshi Nakamoto

alt: A Merkle tree with four data blocks L1 to L4 at the bottom. Each is hashed, pairs of hashes are hashed again to give Hash 0 and Hash 1, and those two give the Top Hash at the top.
author: Azaghal

alt: A Merkle tree with three data blocks L1, L2 and L3. L3 has no partner, so its hash is drawn twice (the copy in a dashed box) and the two copies are combined into Hash 1.
author: MrTsepa

alt: A Merkle tree of four data blocks where L3 is coloured orange. The hashes needed to check L3, which are hash of L4 and Hash 0, are yellow. The hashes on the path from L3 up to the Top Hash are green.
author: MrTsepa

alt: A radix tree storing the words Peter, Peck, Peppers, Piper, Picked and Pickled. Each edge carries a piece of text, so shared beginnings such as P, e and i are stored once and the words split where they differ.
author: Cmglee

alt: A chain of black blocks drawn from a green block at the bottom upward. Two side branches of purple blocks leave the main chain and stop, showing blocks that are not part of the main chain.
author: Michele 93

alt: Two panels with generals around a castle. On the left six generals all attack with red arrows. On the right four generals attack and two grey generals retreat with blue arrows, so the attack is not coordinated.
author: Lord Belbury

alt: A client and a server exchange seven numbered steps: request service, choose, challenge, solve, response, verify and grant service. The client does the solving work and the server only verifies.
author: Fabien Coelho

alt: A bar chart of stacked bitcoin coins. The block reward falls from 50 to 25, then 12.5, then 6.25, with a note that it halves every 4 years until depletion.
author: Heslovar

alt: A line chart of total bitcoins in existence from 2009 to 2026. It rises steeply at first and then flattens as it approaches 21 million.
author: FrankAndProust

alt: A line chart of Bitcoin mining difficulty from 2009 to 2026 on a logarithmic scale. It rises from 1 to more than ten to the fourteenth power, fastest in the early years.
author: FrankAndProust

alt: A Bitmain Antminer S9, a box-shaped ASIC bitcoin miner with a large fan at the front and an exhaust duct, standing next to its separate power supply.
author: Steve Rainwater

alt: A crossed-out box of bitcoin coins above a box of key pairs. A Bitcoin wallet does not hold coins; it holds pairs of private and public keys.
author: Matthäus Wander

alt: The stack after each step of a Pay to Public Key Hash script: signature, public key, OP_DUP, OP_HASH160, the expected public key hash, OP_EQUALVERIFY and OP_CHECKSIG, ending with the value true.
author: Anthonyceegp

alt: A line chart of daily Ethereum transactions from 2016 to 2024. It starts near zero, climbs to about 1.3 million in early 2018, dips, and then stays around 1 to 1.2 million a day, with a few spikes near 2 million.
author: J0rd1
